column3: Direct peg imagery frames mountains as stabilizing supports; their later removal keeps that stability functional rather than inherent.
Mountains prevent sway while rivers and paths remain usable, pairing stability with movement and orientation.
The ark's course and mooring preserve the parallel reading of divinely governed movement and fixed arrival.
Earth and mountains crushed together shows even the highest, hardest stabilizers can lose their distinction.
The preceding spreading of the earth supplies the surface that 79:32 then anchors with mountains.
Anchored mountains and open passes jointly present a terrain made stable without becoming impassable.
Mountains and earth quake, and firm mass becomes loose sand, sharply contrasting 79:32's emplacement.
The Hour's mursa anchors the secondary temporal-mooring reading alongside mountains' spatial anchoring.
Mountains are pulverized, making their firmness in 79:32 a bestowed and reversible condition.
The mountains' refusal to bear the trust separates material magnitude from moral capacity.
Its nearness-of-term theme only indirectly supports the temporal-anchorage reading associated with the Hour.
Mountains serve as the measure of extreme resistance, clarifying the force implied by their emplacement.

Blown-away mountains show that their stabilizing role has a term and can be withdrawn.

A mountain lifted overhead overturns its normal fixedness and turns physical mass into a covenantal warning.

The commanded descent and blessing after the ark's settlement continue the channel of arrival, fixed place, and renewed life.
A mountain imagined humbled and split reverses hardness, making it a forceful contrast to emplacement.

The strong built structure above supplies a structural frame that sits beside 78:7 and 79:32.
Mountains made to move and become a mirage directly negate their apparent firmness.

Earth placed for living beings supports the provision-oriented end of the surrounding earth-and-mountains ordering.
